Given that $r$, $s$ and $t$ in the above diagram are parallel, find $m∠1.$
question.worked_solution:
Consider $∠2$ in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14246974/assets/5afb2a0f9f26dc3c02b52ac50743e9541f587349267b0c322cb2644b09c48617.png)

Notice that $∠2$ and the angle whose measure is ${66}^{∘}$ are alternate exterior angles formed when the transversal $v$ cuts the parallel lines $r$ and $s.$ Hence, 

$$
m∠2={66}^{∘}.
$$

Also, notice that the angle determined by $∠1$ and $∠2$ and the angle whose measure is ${127}^{∘}$ are corresponding angles formed when the transversal $u$ cuts the parallel lines $s$ and $t.$ Hence, 

$$
m∠1+m∠2={127}^{∘}.
$$

Now, substituting $m∠2$ into the equation, we can find $m∠1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠1+m∠2 & ={127}^{∘} \\ m∠1+{66}^{∘} & ={127}^{∘} \\ m∠1 & ={61}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$
